candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall collect a minimum of three samples (flow-weighted composite if possible) from the outfall(s).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether 'if possible' makes flow-weighted composite sampling mandatory or discretionary affects whether the three-sample collection requirement was satisfied for FY2025 monitoring obligations.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall collect a second and third sample (composite samples if possible) for use during the 24-hour renewal of each dilution concentration for each test.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of when composite samples are required for dilution renewals, and how many renewals each test entails, affects whether required toxicity sampling protocols were applicable and met.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee must collect the composite samples so that the maximum holding time for any effluent sample shall not exceed 36 hours for first use of the sample. The permittee must have initiated the toxicity test within 36 hours after the collection of the last portion of the first composite sample.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of the 36-hour initiation and first-use deadlines could change whether sampling and testing met permit conditions (B) and whether resulting data are valid or should be treated as missing or procedurally deficient evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: A holding time up to 72 hrs is allowed upon notification to EPA and NMED of the need for additional holding time.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether notification occurred and whether the 72-hour extension applies affects whether extended holding complied with monitoring requirements (B) and whether tests conducted under that extension count as valid reported evidence or unresolved procedural exceptions (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee must collect the composite samples such that the effluent samples are representative of the discharge duration, and of any periodic episode of chlorination, biocide usage or other potentially toxic substance discharged on an intermittent basis.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether intermittent chlorination, biocide use, or other toxic episodes occurred, and whether sampling captured them, affects when representative sampling was required (B) and whether absent or untimed samples reflect conditional non-requirement, documented no-discharge, or missing evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: for every valid or invalid toxicity test initiated, whether carried to completion or not.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The scope of tests covered by full-report preparation obligations turns on what counts as initiated, valid, invalid, or incomplete; different interpretations change required reporting (B) and how missing or partial test records are classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: For any test which fails, is considered invalid, or which is terminated early for any reason, the full report must be submitted for agency review.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Classification of a test as failed, invalid, or early-terminated triggers a mandatory submission obligation (B) and determines whether the case is documented noncompliance, procedurally invalid data, or missing adequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: A valid test for each species must be reported during each reporting period specified in PART I of this permit unless the permittee is performing a TRE which may increase the frequency of testing and reporting.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Applicability depends on cross-referenced PART I reporting periods, species covered, and whether a TRE was underway; different readings change which valid-test reporting obligations applied in FY2025 (B) and whether absent results reflect non-requirement, increased-frequency TRE monitoring, or missing evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: One set of biomonitoring data for each species is to be recorded on the DMR for each reporting period.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which species and reporting periods require a DMR-recorded biomonitoring result affects the measurement set available for any numeric limit comparison (A), establishes a reporting obligation per species per period (B), and frames whether absent DMR entries are missing required evidence or another documented state (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall submit the results of each valid toxicity test on the subsequent monthly DMR for that reporting period as follows below. Submit retest information clearly marked as such with the following month's DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'subsequent monthly DMR,' reporting-period alignment, and retest deferral to the following month affects whether timely reporting was required and met (B) and whether delayed or unmarked retests appear as missing, misclassified, or unresolved evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Only results of valid tests are to be reported on the DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a test is valid determines which toxicity results appear on the DMR for compliance evaluation (A) and whether non-DMR invalid tests should be treated as documented invalid data, conditional non-reporting, or missing adequate evidence rather than ordinary numeric results (C).
